sylvia: Heads-up — venice13b-int4 canary is hitting intermittent OOMs in prod during longer completions. Started after kernel swap to the new fused-attn path + quant rollout. stack snippet:

```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 31.88 GiB total capacity; 28.4 GiB already allocated; 512 MiB free; 29.75 GiB reserved by PyTorch)
  at /build/runtime/runner.cc:142
```

sylvia: Repro locally with max_new_tokens=512 + batch_size=4 triggers it reliably; with max_new_tokens=256 it completes. Any ideas? :thinking_face:

ben: thanks for flagging. first thought: kernel path may use extra workspace for fused-attn at large seqs. did you try forcing the older attention kernel?

sylvia: not yet. can push a quick canary to fallback to torch_attention to test.

maria: fwiw quant int4 increases activation buffering in our current allocator because of alignment padding we added. long generations amplify that.

ben: ok — 2 quick experiments that helped before: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens for venice13b to 256 in onboarding config, 2) set kernel_affinity: [torch_attn] for requests > 300 tokens so fused path doesn't get picked.

sylvia: i'll try 1 locally now.

(tariq joined the thread)

tariq: if you want a faster A/B: we can flip the runtime policy to prefer the legacy kernel for canary model id venice13b-int4. i'll patch routing config for a minute.

sylvia: patched locally: with `--max_new_tokens 512 --batch-size 4` + `kernel_override=legacy` passes. With fused path fails. confirms kernel difference.

ben: great. can we also check if KV cache prefetch is increasing peak mem? disable kv_prefetch for the canary and rerun.

sylvia: turning off kv_prefetch drops peak by ~1.1 GiB. looks promising.

maria: that matches theory — quantized kernels + prefetch touch extra buffers for cache priming. also our compaction heuristics don't trigger until allocation bounce, so fragmentation gets worse on long gens.

dmitri: action items: (A) short-term: set venice13b default max_new_tokens=256 and temporarily disable kv_prefetch in model config. (B) mid-term: add kernel_fallback policy for >300 new tokens to prefer torch_attn. (C) long-term: update allocator compaction thresholds and evaluate fused kernel workspace accounting for quantized layouts.

sylvia: i've opened an onboarding patch with (A) + kv change: PR #3421. link: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/3421 - includes test harness reproducer.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary config update for venice13b-int4 to roll in 10m. CI checks: green.

tariq: i'll do (B) — small runtime policy change, will canary to 10% traffic. leaves QA window.

ben: also we should update docs and the per-model tuning guide to note that int4 fused kernels may need extra headroom for generations >300 tokens. small blurb in onboarding checklist.

maria: pinging infra-research to add a quick instrument to record fused kernel workspace usage per request. we need telemetry to avoid guessing in future.

sylvia: after the patch + kv toggle, canary ran 6 hrs with no OOMs at traffic levels that previously failed. will keep monitoring.

dmitri: great. schedule card for allocator compaction tuning next sprint. I'll assign to @maria and @dmitri.

sylvia: summary for ops notes: changed venice13b defaults: max_new_tokens=256, kv_prefetch=false; runtime kernel fallback for >300 tokens in flight; PR #3421 deployed to canary. keeping this thread open for 24h monitoring. :thumbsup:

ben: nice detective work. :tada:

maria: thanks all.

ops-bot: Monitoring alert rule created: `venice13b-int4_peak_oom_rate` -> notify eng-ml if >1/hour.

sylvia: closing loop soon but marking action done for now.
